Subject: Operator access & key control for VPC private deployment

Irene —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we move to procurement we need to confirm a few privacy/security points specific to the private (VPC / on-prem) deployment option:

1) Will any Redwood operator or subprocessors have the ability to access customer plaintext or model inputs/outputs in the deployed environment? We need a clear guarantee that customer data at rest and in transit is not accessible by Redwood staff.

2) For customer-managed keys (CMEK), is Redwood asking for any escrow, escrow-withdrawal triggers, or operator break-glass that would allow retrieval of keys? If so, please describe the legal threshold and technical controls.

3) Please provide the current subprocessors list and identify any that would be onshore vs offshore. Acme requires US-only subprocessors for production PHI handling.

4) What logs/telemetry does Redwood collect from a private deploy, how long are they retained, and can we get an ingest-only view (no decrypted content)?

5) DPA/Contract language: do you have recommended redlines for custody/keystore clauses, and any precedents where you accepted controller requirements for key sovereignty?

We'd like to get answers in writing this week so procurement can schedule DocuSign with Legal. If any of this requires a short technical call, happy to do 30 min on Monday.

Thanks,
Michael

Irene —

Attached is a short "operator trust model" (privdep_trust_model_v1.pdf) that lays out:

- Roles & privileges: operator-support (non-privileged), infra-ops (maintenance), security-sre (incident response). Each role mapped to allowed actions and evidence trails.
- CMEK flow: customers may supply an external KMS or use our recommended HSM. In the external KMS case Redwood never has key material. For HSM/CMEK we support a remote-wrap flow where Redwood holds only an encrypted key blob and is unable to decrypt without a customer-signed release token.
- Break-glass: we propose a two-party approval for any emergency key release (customer admin + Redwood security lead), logged to an immutable audit trail. Legal triggers for release would be limited to a court order or explicitly agreed recovery clause in the DPA.
- Telemetry: we separate health/billing metrics (aggregated counts, token counts, latency) from request payload logs. Request payloads are never stored in plaintext in hosted or private by default; debug logs that contain payloads are gated and available only if the customer opts in and grants ephemeral key access.

Immediate recommendations for the DPA (short):
1) Processor will not access customer plaintext. Any operator access to request/response data requires documented customer approval or a court order.
2) Customer maintains exclusive control of encryption keys; Redwood will not escrow keys except under a narrowly defined legal escrow with explicit customer consent and written process (describe triggers).
3) Subprocessors providing on-prem install support will be limited to named vendors; any change must be pre-notified and approved for US-only requirement.
4) Audit logs for operator actions will be retained for 2 years and provided to customer on request for compliance review.

Next steps: I can refine the PDF into two short paragraphs the legal team can paste into the DPA. Marcus — can you confirm the minimum operator permissions for routine maintenance (patching, health checks) and the mechanisms to do so without access to plaintext?

-Karthik

Team —

I reviewed Karthik's model. From a contract perspective we should offer the following redlines (concise, meant to be pasted into the customer's DPA):

1) Keystore & Key Sovereignty (new clause): "Customer retains exclusive control over cryptographic keys used to encrypt Customer Data. Redwood shall not possess or derive plaintext key material. Any request for escrow or key release will require documented Customer consent and either a court order or the dual-approval emergency process described in Schedule X."

2) Subprocessors & Geo: "Redwood will only engage subprocessors listed in Schedule Y. For Customer environments processing PHI, Redwood will ensure onshore-only subprocessors and will obtain Customer written consent prior to engaging new subprocessors in-scope for PHI."

3) Operator Access & Break-Glass: "Operator access to Customer Data is prohibited except as expressly authorized by Customer or as compelled by law. Emergency access is permitted under the dual-approval break-glass process and will be logged, time-limited, and subject to post-incident review."

4) Telemetry & Logs: "Redwood will provide aggregated health and billing telemetry by default. Request/response payloads are not retained unless Customer opts in. Operator debug access to payloads is only possible via a documented ephemeral process requiring Customer authorization."

5) Audit & Evidence: "Redwood will retain operator action audit logs for a minimum of 24 months and make them available for Customer review upon reasonable request subject to redaction for third-party personal data."

I attached a short excerpt (redwood_dpa_excerpt.docx) with clause text and a proposed Schedule X/Y layout. If Acme counters with no escrow at all we can accept that for a higher SLA/price point — flagging this to Sales.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Michael —

Thanks for the clear list. Internal summary below and attachments with proposed DPA language. Short version: we can meet Acme's US-only and key-sovereignty asks with the following commitments (draft language attached):

- No operator access to plaintext: Redwood will not access or derive plaintext customer data in private deployments unless explicitly authorized by the customer or compelled by a valid court order. (See clause in redwood_dpa_excerpt.docx)
- Customer-controlled keys: Customers may supply/externalize KMS keys. Redwood will support an external KMS flow where we never hold key material. For HSM/CMEK options where Redwood assists with key lifecycle, key release is gated by a documented dual-approval break-glass (Customer admin + Redwood security lead) and will require either customer consent or a court order.
- Subprocessors & geo: For PHI environments we will restrict subprocessors to those listed in Schedule Y (US-only). Any new subprocessors in-scope for PHI require written Customer consent.
- Telemetry: Default telemetry is aggregated health and billing metrics only. Request/response payloads are not stored unless Customer enables debug logs; such access is ephemeral and must be explicitly granted by the Customer via an approval flow.
- Auditability: Operator actions are logged and retained for 24 months; audit extracts can be provided for compliance reviews on request.

Attachments: privdep_trust_model_v1.pdf, redwood_dpa_excerpt.docx.

Next steps: 1) If this looks acceptable, can Acme Legal review the attached redline and mark comments this week? 2) If you want a walk-through of the trust model, Karthik and Marcus can do a 30-min technical call Tuesday morning (PST). 3) Procurement: I'll prep a DocuSign package with the DPA schedule once we have agreement on the key/escrow language.
